[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] Serverfarm describes itself as a global data center developer and operator with more than 25 years of operating experience, focused on AI-ready, build-to-suit, high-density facilities. The operators homepage did not state a headquarters address, exact founding year, or ownership structure.

The companys site lists nine operational North American locations, Clarksville, Atlanta, Chicago, two in Houston, Los Angeles, Northern Virginia, Moses Lake, Washington, and Toronto, Canada, plus three in Europe and the Middle East, Amsterdam, London, and two in Israel, with additional sites described as coming soon. Trade press and Serverfarms own press release describe the company acquiring a 12 megawatt Los Angeles data center in El Segundo from T5 Data Centers, another operator separately tracked in this registry, for approximately $71 million, a direct example of a facility changing hands between two operators already profiled here.

The registry here tracks 2 Serverfarm facilities across two states, California and Illinois. The California facility is a strong candidate to be the same El Segundo, Los Angeles building acquired from T5, a specific lead this registrys facility-level research phase should verify directly rather than treat as a fresh Serverfarm build, recording a former_operator relationship to T5 if confirmed. This facility is recorded under the operator name Serverfarm LLC in this registry, treated as the same entity as Serverfarm researched at the operator level. This research was carried out at the operator level in an earlier phase of this project.

reading.body:
This facility has no published power specification in the data provided, so its scale relative to California's mapped AI infrastructure cannot be determined. The state context shows 103 mapped facilities in California, of which only 11 publish power figures totaling 365 megawatts, meaning most operators in the state do not disclose capacity. This facility ranks 12th by published megawatts in California, but that ranking reflects only the small fraction of sites with disclosed specs.

The research notes indicate Serverfarm acquired a 12-megawatt data center in El Segundo from T5 Data Centers around 2024, and this facility may be that same building. If so, it represents a transfer of existing capacity rather than new build, and the 12-megawatt figure would apply here, though it is not published in this facility's own spec section. At typical AI training densities of roughly 40 kilowatts per rack, 12 megawatts of IT load would support approximately 300 racks. The facility's published certifications and current tenant mix are not stated in the data.

Serverfarm operates nine North American locations across four countries and describes itself as focused on AI-ready, high-density builds. The company has a track record of acquiring and operating existing facilities rather than only building new ones, as shown by the T5 acquisition. The state context shows California has significant unmapped or unspecified data center capacity beyond the 365 megawatts published, so this facility's actual importance to regional AI compute may differ substantially from what published figures reveal.
